note: An anchored additional physical delivery adds the documented column to the named version beside the native variable's other columns of that version, which keep their own states; it copies no documented type, and only an explicit storage header types it. The [[identity.partition]] maps give each column its owner (without them the native variable has several spellings and is withheld). Expected literals: the sibling states (OTHER and SECOND 2020, EARLIER 2018) and the added ADD 2020 state from preserves_siblings (column names VALUE/OTHER/SECOND/EARLIER kept; addition column VALUE); ADD 2020 data_type null from preserves_siblings and storage_header[None] (data_type None); ADDP 2020 text from storage_header[PHYSICAL] (CIS2020 PHYSICAL varchar -> text). Both entries apply without a blocker or stale entry (preserves_siblings: `not converted.blockers`, `not applied.diagnostics`). The drift halves of preserves_siblings ([field], [parent], [missing], [new]) have no build form for this entry: [[errata.delivered]] carries no expected-fields or parent-fact guard, so drift in a sibling's facts does not stale it (a changed sibling definition still applies it), and a missing or new sibling column stales this case's [[identity.partition]] map (its column set no longer matches), not the delivered entry (probed with the sibling's definition changed, the sibling removed and a new var-27 column added). That partition drift is pinned in split-partition-native-stale-when-a-reviewed-column-is-missing and split-partition-native-stale-when-an-unreviewed-column-is-added.
fails_if: `scb_errata.convert_delivered_entry` rewrites the target version's sibling rows to the added column (drops the `matching and additional_physical_column` branch), copies the donor's documented type into the addition, or looks storage up by the entry column instead of `storage_column`
